name: OTDC Panthanivas Taptapani Restaurant
signature_dish: Fresh local fish and country chicken in Odia style
why_it_matters: The restaurant at the OTDC Panthanivas — sitting roughly 300m from the Taptapani hot sulphur spring — is the only proper sit-down dining at this remote hill destination in Ganjam district. Run by the Odisha Tourism Development Corporation, it serves Indian, Chinese and continental dishes; fresh local fish and country chicken in Odia style are the specialities visitors most recommend, with hill views from the dining area.
insider_tip: Place your food order in advance and visit the hot spring while it cooks — the kitchen is slow and the menu depends on what stock arrived that day. Fresh fish and country chicken are the dishes to ask for; veg options can be limited. It pairs naturally with a Taptapani-Daringbadi hill circuit.
signature_address: OTDC Panthanivas, Taptapani, Pudamari, Ganjam district, Odisha 761014

name: Taptapani road dhaba cluster (Berhampur-Phulbani highway)
signature_dish: Roadside Odia thali and egg curry on the hill highway
why_it_matters: Taptapani sits on the State Highway linking Berhampur with western Odisha, and small roadside dhabas and tea stalls along this hill stretch serve the steady traffic of travellers heading between Berhampur, Taptapani and the Daringbadi hills. With no restaurants beyond the Panthanivas at the spring itself, these dhabas are the honest budget option for a quick meal.
insider_tip: These are simple highway dhabas, not named destination restaurants — pick the busiest one with hot food coming off the stove. Best for a tea, egg curry and rice break rather than a leisurely meal. For anything more, the Panthanivas restaurant at the spring is the only sit-down choice.
signature_address: State Highway, Taptapani, Sanakhemundi block, Ganjam district, Odisha 761014
